Samantha — thanks for sending and for the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (privacy counsel) and Karthik (sales lead) so we can respond on legal substance and execution logistics.

Quick high-level:
- We can accept SCCs as the lawful mechanism for transfers and propose a short EU addendum referencing the standard SCC clauses rather than embedding them in the DPA. Will Marissa confirm?
- Regarding audit cooperation: we typically offer remote audit rights with scoped evidence requirements; we avoid open-ended on-site audits for security/contractual reasons. Marissa, can you suggest wording that addresses their regulatory concern while keeping Redwood's operational controls intact?
- Subprocessors: Redwood posts a running inventory and provides 10 business days' notice for material changes. We do not permit termination for all subprocessor additions, only for material data-flow related changes or breaches.

Execution path: we prefer DocuSign for standard DPAs (audit trail + delegated signing). Karthik — can you confirm whether we should route via Sales > Legal > Finance for countersignature, or use the standard authorizer (Head of Revenue) on this mid-market deal? Also confirm any discount/credit ask so procurement can evaluate holistically.

I'll wait for Marissa on precise redline language and then propose a cleaned counter to AlliedHealth.

Best,

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: DPA redlines (initial) + subprocessor inventory

Logan / Karthik — I reviewed AlliedHealth's redline and attached a short comment set (redline-comments-mc.pdf) with our suggested compromise language. Highlights:

1) Section 7 (Audits) — Proposed compromise: remote audit with pre-defined data scopes, 30 days' notice, and a right to redact IP/operationally sensitive material. If they need on-site, we can offer it as a paid additional service with an agreed SOP.

2) Section 9 (Subprocessors) — We will confirm the current inventory (I reviewed their CSV). We accept the 10 business day notice for material additions. We won't accept a blanket termination right; counterproposal: termination only if Redwood materially changes the types of processing or a breach occurs that we cannot remediate in 30 days. I've added specific language.

3) Section 11 (Transfers / SCCs) — We can include an annex referencing the SCCs and commit to implementation of appropriate technical and organizational safeguards. Suggest adding migration to updated SCCs as industry practice evolves.

4) Liability / caps — Allied's redline increased caps for security incidents. Recommend keeping standard commercial cap (2x fees for twelve months) and adding carveouts for willful misconduct.

Next steps I recommend:
- Logan to send AlliedHealth a clean countersigned-language draft with our tracked changes (I can produce the tracked doc).
- Karthik to confirm signatory and whether Finance needs to run a credit hold.
- If Allied insists on on-site audits, we escalate to Sales + Legal to review a paid engagement model.

I've attached redline-comments-mc.pdf and flagged the three clause hotspots. I'll be available tomorrow morning to jump on a quick 20-minute call with Allied counsel if needed.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: redline-comments-mc.pdf (annotated comments, 18KB)
